headline.text: Kymenlaakso lags national benchmarks in crude curative treatment at 19.3% (95% CI 16.3–22.7) versus 27.0% and recorded MDT meetings at 0.5% (95% CI 0.2–1.5) versus 6.0%.

details.text: Crude curative treatment, which is not adjusted for age or stage, was 19.3% (95% CI 16.3–22.7; n=114/591) in Kymenlaakso compared with 27.0% (4009/14873) nationally, and its 95% confidence interval excludes the national value.

In figures digitised from Kuva 16 for curative treatment only, by sex (precision ±0.5 percentage points), the gap holds after age adjustment for men at 17.9% (95% CI 13.9–22.9) versus 26.7% nationally (95% CI excludes 26.7%), whereas for women at 22.6% (95% CI 16.8–29.3) versus 26.9% the 95% confidence interval includes the national value.

Across overlapping treatment categories where a patient can receive several types, crude shares exceeded national values, with 95% confidence intervals excluding national benchmarks for life-prolonging treatment at 37.6% (95% CI 33.8–41.5; n=222/591) versus 30.4% (4522/14873) and symptomatic treatment at 51.3% (95% CI 47.2–55.3; n=303/591) versus 39.5% (5871/14873).

An MDT meeting was recorded for 0.5% (95% CI 0.2–1.5; n=3/591) of patients versus 6.0% (893/14873) nationally, with the 95% confidence interval excluding the national value, though HILMO captures procedures only from direct patient contacts so this measures recording practice rather than care.

headline.text: A below-national no-treatment-record share suggests the curative gap is not only a recording artefact, though missing stage data and unmeasured pathway waits leave causes unclear.

details.text: The crude share with no treatment record within 12 months, mixing untreated patients and unrecorded treatment, was 16.4% (95% CI 13.7–19.6; n=97/591) versus 27.5% (4089/14873) nationally (95% CI excludes 27.5%); as an inference, this data-quality signal is consistent with relatively complete treatment recording (though not direct evidence of it), making the low curative share less likely to be only a recording artefact.

Although a journal article found that HILMO diagnoses match the Cancer Registry for about 90% of most cancer types (which concerns diagnosis concordance only and not treatment, referral or MDT recording), Finland has no cancer quality registry and stage at diagnosis is widely missing nationally, preventing stage adjustment of county shares.

Public registry data do not measure symptom onset, exclude outpatient primary care and occupational health visits, omit referral dates, capture imaging only when it is the sole basis of diagnosis (in about 20% of cases nationally), and show whether specialist visits or treatments occurred within 12 months but not when they started.

Preliminary, unpublished national figures report an average of 155 days from symptoms to initial treatment in Finland—comprising 56 days of patient delay, 41 days in primary care, and 58 days in specialist care—compared with 107 days in Sweden and 67 days in Denmark, though these preliminary national averages are not county-specific.

headline.text: Kymenlaakso can track pathway access times using THL 21/2016 definitions, standardise primary care referrals and diagnostic coordination, and audit MDT and stage recording completeness.

details.text: Because the Health Care Act sets no maximum wait for a cancer suspicion and Finland lacks uniform diagnostic timetables, Kymenlaakso can track access times using THL Ohjaus 21/2016 guidance (covering 16 cancers) with handover alerts while the roadmap plans national target times by 2026–2028 and Filha's diagnostics guideline is due before the 2030 evaluation.

Because mentor insight notes that a weak referral receives a lower urgency rating in specialist care, Kymenlaakso can update its local referral instructions with a required-content template and a rule to refer persistent unexplained symptoms despite a clear X-ray, as in the KYS regional pathway document, while the roadmap plans national referral criteria in 2026–2028.

Assigning a named contact person for the diagnostic phase—which none of the reviewed regional pathway documents include—gives patients a clear contact point while the national roadmap maps which care stage to target and plans care-coordinator guidance in 2026–2028 for counties to adopt in 2029–2031.

Kymenlaakso can also audit and report how completely it records stage at diagnosis and MDT meetings—currently logged in HILMO for 0.5% (95% CI 0.2–1.5; n=3/591) of patients versus 6.0% (893/14873) nationally—aligning with national plans for uniform recording instructions and a cancer quality registry targeting 90% coverage including stage.
